log.why: Testing {fliC, gyrA} (0.450 combined prior) splits the probability mass nearly in half for maximum information gain.
Testing 3 uM splits Ticket 2's prior probability mass nearly in half (0.612 vs 0.388) while Ticket 1's plate incubates.
Knocking out metJ tests the 0.548 leading hypothesis directly, splitting posterior mass nearly 50/50 and likely enabling immediate publication if confirmed.
E2 splits Ticket 2's posterior nearly in half (0.582 vs 0.418) and strongly tests 3 uM against lower thresholds.
Ticket 3 is highly uncertain, and testing at 10 µM splits its probability mass nearly in half (0.438 vs 0.562) before publishing.
Posterior for metJ is 0.932 after two plates, making immediate publication optimal to preserve time and plate bonuses and free a ticket slot.
E5 splits the remaining posterior mass nearly evenly (0.44 vs 0.56) and uses a free incubator before publishing Ticket 2.
E2 negative and E3 positive strongly bracket 3 µM at 0.730 posterior, securing points before expiry and opening a ticket slot.
Testing at 100 µM cleanly separates the two leading hypotheses (100 µM at 0.540 vs 300 µM at 0.379) before Ticket 3's deadline.
Ticket 4 is urgent with flat priors; E11 bisects the posterior (0.473 probability) while Ticket 3's decisive E6 finishes incubating.
Testing fliC resolves the narrow lead between hisG and fliC after E11 while leaving time to publish Ticket 3 during incubation.
Ticket 3 has only 11s left and a strong 0.814 posterior for 100 uM, so we must publish before expiration.
With 11 seconds left, no new plate can finish; publishing hisG at 0.580 posterior beats expiration.
Knock out {trpE, araC} to test the top two culprit candidates holding 61.4% of the prior mass before pairing a second split.
Pairing E6 {rpoB, trpE} with growing E8 {trpE, araC} orthogonally separates the top four gene candidates before the round ends.
With only 6 seconds left in the round, no experiment can finish, and araC has a strong 0.855 posterior.
With 1 s left in the round and low posteriors (max 0.264), no experiment or publication can finish cleanly.
